business_problem: High-volume turnover in the Chaplain Corps and routine chapel administration made resource, maintenance, facilities, and transition work disruptive and pulled chaplains and religious support specialists away from spiritual readiness work.
solution_summary: The U.S. Army Chaplain Corps, through Maj. Sean Callahan, built the Chaplain Administrative Platform (CHAP) as an in-house AI agent and dashboard during the Command and General Staff College AI Basics elective. The article describes CHAP as a no-code, replicable tool for chapel community administrative management that automates day-to-day work around resources, supply, maintenance, facilities, and related decision support. Its implementation is grounded in prompt engineering and use of Large Language Models, with the builder iterating prompts and guardrails across different LLMs to improve outputs. CHAP is intended to convert tacit institutional knowledge into explicit, reusable guidance that can transfer between posts with minimal deviation, while presenting actionable information to chaplains, religious support specialists, and commanders. The source does not identify a model vendor, storage architecture, or named external integrations.

solution_components.name: Chaplain Administrative Platform (CHAP)
solution_components.role: An in-house AI agent and dashboard that automates chapel administrative management and supports leadership decisions.

solution_components.name: Large Language Models
solution_components.role: LLMs underpin the prompt-driven AI behavior and were used to refine prompts, gaps, and guardrails for the agent.

business_outcome: CHAP automated administrative tasks, gave time back to chaplains and religious support specialists, reduced disruption during personnel transitions, preserved institutional knowledge, and helped inform commanders' finance and facilities decisions.
architecture_clues: Built in just a few weeks during the U.S. Army Command and General Staff College AI Basics elective.
Described as a replicable AI agent and a no-code software product.
The article shows CHAP dashboard pages including Supply Management.
Designed to be transferable between posts with very little deviation to reduce turnover-related disruption.
